dcSweep.explanation: Steps one ideal grounded voltage source through evenly spaced DC values and reports the steady node voltages of a resistor network (capacitors act as open circuits). Outputs are results.csv (source voltage, then one column per probe in volts), circuit-summary.json and the generated netlist circuit.cir; every native value is checked against an independent nodal solution. Choose it for dividers, bridges and other resistive networks; use acSweep for frequency response and rcStep for a charging curve.
pitfalls: start and stop are source volts and stop must exceed start; points includes both endpoints.
Every node needs a path through resistors to ground or the source; a node reached only through capacitors is rejected as floating.
Only ideal resistors and capacitors; semiconductors, models, subcircuits and imported netlists are not accepted.

examples.purpose: Verify a resistive divider across six source voltages.
Apply named finite-sample acceptance and inspect observed worst conditions.

acSweep.explanation: Characterise bounded ideal linear RLC networks across linear, decade or octave frequencies: native node voltages, optional native source-current/KCL checks, derived input impedance and passive branch complex power. Declare peak/RMS phasor convention and sampled gain, relative phase, current, power or loading requirements. Results retain verified CSV, circuit summary and inspectable netlist. Use for filters, source loading, resonance and resistor heating; no nonlinear or general transient claim.
pitfalls: For logarithmic spacing points is nominal samples per decade/octave, not total output count; actual count must fit3–512.
Declare peak or rms amplitude convention before interpreting power; currents are a to b and input current is -i(vdrive). Branch current is derived, whereas input current is native observed.
Phase requirements use principal relative Vprobe/Vsource angle and refuse zero response. A bound never wraps and solver tolerance does not relax user acceptance.
Every frequency must have a nonsingular, conditioned network; no ideal-inductor/source loops, mutual coupling, nonlinear models or continuous-envelope guarantee.

examples.purpose: Verify the analytic RC cutoff and phase lag.
Verify an RL low-pass at and above cutoff.
Verify capacitor voltage in a damped series RLC circuit at and above resonance.
Verify a resistor-fed parallel LC band-pass across resonance.
Apply named finite-sample acceptance and inspect observed worst conditions.
Declare sampled gain/phase/loading/heating goals and inspect passive electrical metrics on a logarithmic grid.

rcStep.explanation: Simulates an initially uncharged series resistor feeding a grounded capacitor when a constant voltage is switched on at t = 0, and reports the source and capacitor node voltages at evenly spaced times. Native transient values are resampled and checked against V x (1 - exp(-t/RC)). Outputs match the other analyses (results.csv with time in seconds, summary and netlist). Choose it for RC charging and settling-time checks only.
pitfalls: The circuit must be exactly source - resistor - response node - capacitor - ground; any other topology fails with UNSUPPORTED_CIRCUIT.
stop (seconds) must lie between 0.01 and 20 time constants R x C; the default 0.005 s suits only RC values near 0.25 to 500 ms.
The default probe is "out"; name the capacitor node "out" or list the actual node in probes.

examples.purpose: Verify a 5 V RC charging curve across five time constants.
Apply named finite-sample acceptance and inspect observed worst conditions.

fields.explanation: An ideal linear circuit driven by one grounded voltage source, the analysis to run (dcSweep, acSweep or rcStep) and optional voltage or gain requirements checked at the computed samples. The circuit is written inline; no netlist, device model or script can be imported.

/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis circuit document; it must be "schemaxis.ngspice/1". It is not the ngspice release.

/properties/operation.explanation: Select dcSweep for steady signed voltage, acSweep for phasor response, or rcStep for initially uncharged first-order settling.

/properties/operation/anyOf/0.explanation: dcSweep: steady-state node voltages of a resistor network while the source steps through a voltage range.

/properties/operation/anyOf/1.explanation: acSweep: magnitude and phase of node voltages versus frequency for a linear R, L, C network.

/properties/operation/anyOf/2.explanation: rcStep: charging curve of one series resistor and grounded capacitor after a voltage step at t = 0.

/properties/circuit.explanation: The circuit, written inline: one ideal voltage source between ground (node "0") and the source node, 1 to 64 resistors, up to 64 capacitors, up to 64 uncoupled inductors (acSweep only) and the nodes to publish. At most 16 non-ground nodes; no netlist, device model or subcircuit can be imported.

/properties/circuit/anyOf/0.explanation: Circuit without inductors, used by dcSweep and rcStep (up to 16 probes). Choose acSweep to use the alternative that also accepts inductors.

/properties/circuit/anyOf/0/properties/s.explanation: Non-ground node driven by the single ideal source referenced to node 0. Use a lowercase identifier; default in. The name gnd in any case is reserved because ngspice rewrites it to ground node 0; use 0 for ground or another name such as gnd1.

/properties/circuit/anyOf/0/properties/r.explanation: Declared ideal resistors with positive resistance in ohms. Each node needs a resistor or AC-inductor reference path to ground or the source.
One ideal resistor with unique name, distinct endpoints and positive ohmic resistance.
Unique lowercase component identifier within the circuit. It labels the generated inspectable netlist; node 0 cannot be a component name.

First terminal node of this component: "0" is ground; any other node is a lowercase letter followed by up to 31 lowercase letters, digits or underscores. a and b must differ. The name gnd in any case is reserved because ngspice rewrites it to ground node 0; use 0 for ground or another name such as gnd1.
Second component endpoint, distinct from a. Uncoupled ideal R, C and L responses do not depend on endpoint ordering.
Positive resistance in ohms, 0.001 to 1e9. Changing resistance changes divider gain or the RC/RL time scale; singular or ill-conditioned networks are rejected.

/properties/circuit/anyOf/0/properties/c.explanation: Ideal capacitors, up to 64, in farads. They are open circuits in dcSweep; rcStep needs exactly one, from the response node to ground.
One ideal capacitor with unique name, distinct endpoints and positive capacitance in farads.
Unique lowercase component identifier within the circuit. It labels the generated inspectable netlist; node 0 cannot be a component name.

Second component endpoint, distinct from a. Uncoupled ideal R, C and L responses do not depend on endpoint ordering.
Positive capacitance in farads, 1e-12 to 1. For example 1e-6 is one microfarad; changing C shifts cutoff and settling time.

/properties/start.explanation: DC start is signed source volts (default 0); AC start is positive frequency Hz (default 1). stop must exceed start. rcStep always starts at zero seconds.

/properties/start/anyOf/0.explanation: First source voltage of the sweep, -1000 to 1000 V. Values from start to stop are evenly spaced, both included; stop must be greater than start.

/properties/start/anyOf/1.explanation: Lowest frequency, 0.001 Hz to 1e9 Hz. Linear spacing includes both endpoints; decade/octave spacing uses nominal density and a partial final interval may end below stop. stop must exceed start.

/properties/stop.explanation: DC stop is source volts (default 5), AC stop is positive Hz (default 10000), RC stop is seconds (default 0.005). RC duration must be 0.01–20 R*C time constants.

/properties/stop/anyOf/0.explanation: Last source voltage of the sweep, -1000 to 1000 V; must be greater than start.

/properties/stop/anyOf/1.explanation: Highest frequency, 0.001 Hz to 1e9 Hz; must be greater than start. Spacing is linear, so a wide range with few points samples low frequencies coarsely.

/properties/stop/anyOf/2.explanation: End time of the step response in seconds (the start is always 0). It must lie between 0.01 and 20 time constants R x C; five time constants show about 99.3% of the final voltage.
pitfalls: With other R or C values the default 0.005 s may fall outside 0.01 to 20 tau and fail planning; set stop explicitly (for example 5 x R x C).

/properties/points.explanation: Sample control, default 101: for linear AC it is total frequencies including endpoints (3–512); for decade/octave it is nominal points per decade/octave and actual count must be 3–512. DC/RC use total uniform samples. Narrow resonances need appropriate density; requirements inspect only sampled points.

/properties/points/anyOf/0.explanation: Number of evenly spaced samples including both endpoints, 2 to 512. More points resolve the curve better; the requirements only see these samples.

/properties/points/anyOf/1.explanation: AC sample control: linear uses 3–512 total frequencies including endpoints; decade/octave uses nominal samples per interval and the actual output must contain 3–512 points. Narrow resonances need appropriate density; requirements inspect only those samples.

/properties/requirements.explanation: Optional named acceptance requirements on checked native samples. A physically valid circuit may miss these bounds and fail with PERFORMANCE_NOT_MET; omitted requirements add no performance gate.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/0.explanation: Requirements for a DC sweep: limits on a probe's signed voltage (voltage_V) over a window of source voltages (sourceVoltage_V).

/properties/requirements/anyOf/0/items.explanation: One DC requirement: a name, a published probe, quantity voltage_V, axis sourceVoltage_V, a window of source voltages and at least one bound.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/0/items/p.explanation: Unique lowercase requirement identifier, up to 64 characters. It names a measured acceptance result and its explained next action.
Select a node already listed in circuit.probes. Requirements use actual independently checked native node voltages.
voltage_V: the probe's signed node voltage in volts. It is the only quantity available in a DC sweep.
Must be sourceVoltage_V: the window is given in source volts.

Inclusive [lower, upper] range of the sweep axis, in source volts, over which the bounds are checked. It must lie inside the declared sweep and contain at least one sample; only those samples are tested. Endpoints equal to a sample coordinate are matched despite tiny floating-point rounding, but no tolerance is added to the voltage or gain bounds.
pitfalls: Behaviour between samples is not checked; increase points if a peak or crossing could fall between them.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/0/items/p.explanation: One finite sample coordinate in the stated axis units; the first is the inclusive lower endpoint, the second the inclusive upper endpoint.

Optional inclusive lower bound in the chosen quantity units. The smallest observed value is the worst lower-bound condition; signed margin is observed minus minimum. Magnitude quantities require nonnegative bounds; voltage, dB, phase and powers retain their signs.

Optional inclusive upper bound in the chosen quantity units. The largest observed value is the worst upper-bound condition; signed margin is maximum minus observed. At least one bound is required; minimum cannot exceed maximum.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/0/items/a.explanation: Lower-bound form: minimum is given, so the smallest sampled value in the window must be at least minimum; maximum may also be given.
Upper-bound form: maximum is given, so the largest sampled value in the window must not exceed maximum; minimum may also be given.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/1.explanation: Named finite-frequency AC acceptance selects a published node, branch or $input quantity, an inclusive sample-containing frequency window and at least one bound. Supports voltage/gain, relative phase/dB, passive branch current/power and input loading. Signed quantities retain polarity and convention; only magnitude bounds must be nonnegative. No continuous-band guarantee.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/1/items.explanation: Named finite-frequency AC acceptance selects a published node, branch or $input quantity, an inclusive sample-containing frequency window and at least one bound. Supports voltage/gain, relative phase/dB, passive branch current/power and input loading. Signed quantities retain polarity and convention; only magnitude bounds must be nonnegative. No continuous-band guarantee.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/1/items/p.explanation: Unique lowercase requirement identifier, up to 64 characters. It names a measured acceptance result and its explained next action.

For voltage/gain/relative-phase quantities, select a node listed in circuit.probes. For current/power select a component listed in circuit.branchProbes or $input with portMetrics; input impedance only accepts $input. Branch metrics derive from verified native voltages; $input current is native -i(vdrive).

Select magnitude_V or gainMagnitude for nonnegative voltage/gain magnitude; gain_dB is 20log10(abs(Vprobe/Vsource)); phase_deg is principal relative phase in [-180,180]. currentMagnitude_A, activePower_W and reactivePower_var select branchProbes or $input; impedanceMagnitude_Ohm selects $input only with portMetrics. dB, phase and power bounds are signed; zero response refuses dB/phase.
Must be frequency_Hz: the window is given in hertz.

Inclusive [lower, upper] range of the sweep axis, in hertz, over which the bounds are checked. It must lie inside the declared sweep and contain at least one sample; only those samples are tested. Endpoints equal to a sample coordinate are matched despite tiny floating-point rounding, but no tolerance is added to the voltage or gain bounds.
pitfalls: Behaviour between samples is not checked; increase points if a peak or crossing could fall between them.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/1/items/p.explanation: Named finite-frequency AC acceptance selects a published node, branch or $input quantity, an inclusive sample-containing frequency window and at least one bound. Supports voltage/gain, relative phase/dB, passive branch current/power and input loading. Signed quantities retain polarity and convention; only magnitude bounds must be nonnegative. No continuous-band guarantee.

Inclusive lower bound in the chosen quantity units (V, V/V, dB, degrees, A, W, var or ohms). Magnitudes are nonnegative; phase/dB/powers preserve sign. Worst condition is the smallest sampled value, and margin is observed minus minimum. No solver tolerance relaxes acceptance.

Inclusive upper bound in the chosen quantity units. Magnitudes are nonnegative; phase/dB/powers preserve sign. Worst condition is the largest sampled value; margin is maximum minus observed. At least one bound is required and minimum cannot exceed maximum.

/properties/requirements/anyOf/1/items/a.explanation: Lower-bound form: minimum is given, so the smallest sampled value in the window must be at least minimum; maximum may also be given.

One AC-only uncoupled ideal coil with unique name, distinct endpoints and positive inductance in henries.
Unique lowercase component identifier within the circuit. It labels the generated inspectable netlist; node 0 cannot be a component name.

First terminal node of this component: "0" is ground; any other node is a lowercase letter followed by up to 31 lowercase letters, digits or underscores. a and b must differ. The name gnd in any case is reserved because ngspice rewrites it to ground node 0; use 0 for ground or another name such as gnd1.
Second component endpoint, distinct from a. Uncoupled ideal R, C and L responses do not depend on endpoint ordering.
Positive uncoupled inductance in henries, 1e-9 to 1e3. Supported only by acSweep, with no mutual coupling or imported models.

/oneOf/1/properties/start.explanation: Lowest frequency, 0.001 Hz to 1e9 Hz. Linear spacing includes both endpoints; decade/octave spacing uses nominal density and a partial final interval may end below stop. stop must exceed start.

/oneOf/1/properties/stop.explanation: Highest frequency, 0.001 Hz to 1e9 Hz; must be greater than start. Spacing is linear, so a wide range with few points samples low frequencies coarsely.

/oneOf/1/properties/points.explanation: Sample control, default 101: for linear AC it is total frequencies including endpoints (3–512); for decade/octave it is nominal points per decade/octave and actual count must be 3–512. DC/RC use total uniform samples. Narrow resonances need appropriate density; requirements inspect only sampled points.

/oneOf/1/properties/amplitude.explanation: Nonzero source phasor/step amplitude in volts, range -1000 to 1000, default 1. In AC amplitudeConvention explicitly interprets phasors as peak (default) or rms and controls power factor. Negative source amplitude reverses native voltage/current phasors while relative transfer phase and power remain consistent. rcStep uses the step height.

/oneOf/1/properties/requirements.explanation: Optional named acceptance requirements on checked native samples. A physically valid circuit may miss these bounds and fail with PERFORMANCE_NOT_MET; omitted requirements add no performance gate.

/oneOf/1/properties/requirements/items.explanation: Named finite-frequency AC acceptance selects a published node, branch or $input quantity, an inclusive sample-containing frequency window and at least one bound. Supports voltage/gain, relative phase/dB, passive branch current/power and input loading. Signed quantities retain polarity and convention; only magnitude bounds must be nonnegative. No continuous-band guarantee.

/oneOf/1/properties/requirements/items/p.explanation: Unique lowercase requirement identifier, up to 64 characters. It names a measured acceptance result and its explained next action.

For voltage/gain/relative-phase quantities, select a node listed in circuit.probes. For current/power select a component listed in circuit.branchProbes or $input with portMetrics; input impedance only accepts $input. Branch metrics derive from verified native voltages; $input current is native -i(vdrive).

Select magnitude_V or gainMagnitude for nonnegative voltage/gain magnitude; gain_dB is 20log10(abs(Vprobe/Vsource)); phase_deg is principal relative phase in [-180,180]. currentMagnitude_A, activePower_W and reactivePower_var select branchProbes or $input; impedanceMagnitude_Ohm selects $input only with portMetrics. dB, phase and power bounds are signed; zero response refuses dB/phase.
Must be frequency_Hz: the window is given in hertz.

Inclusive [lower, upper] range of the sweep axis, in hertz, over which the bounds are checked. It must lie inside the declared sweep and contain at least one sample; only those samples are tested. Endpoints equal to a sample coordinate are matched despite tiny floating-point rounding, but no tolerance is added to the voltage or gain bounds.
pitfalls: Behaviour between samples is not checked; increase points if a peak or crossing could fall between them.

/oneOf/1/properties/requirements/items/p.explanation: Named finite-frequency AC acceptance selects a published node, branch or $input quantity, an inclusive sample-containing frequency window and at least one bound. Supports voltage/gain, relative phase/dB, passive branch current/power and input loading. Signed quantities retain polarity and convention; only magnitude bounds must be nonnegative. No continuous-band guarantee.

Inclusive lower bound in the chosen quantity units (V, V/V, dB, degrees, A, W, var or ohms). Magnitudes are nonnegative; phase/dB/powers preserve sign. Worst condition is the smallest sampled value, and margin is observed minus minimum. No solver tolerance relaxes acceptance.

Inclusive upper bound in the chosen quantity units. Magnitudes are nonnegative; phase/dB/powers preserve sign. Worst condition is the largest sampled value; margin is maximum minus observed. At least one bound is required and minimum cannot exceed maximum.

/oneOf/1/properties/requirements/items/a.explanation: Lower-bound form: minimum is given, so the smallest sampled value in the window must be at least minimum; maximum may also be given.

Named finite-frequency AC acceptance selects a published node, branch or $input quantity, an inclusive sample-containing frequency window and at least one bound. Supports voltage/gain, relative phase/dB, passive branch current/power and input loading. Signed quantities retain polarity and convention; only magnitude bounds must be nonnegative. No continuous-band guarantee.

/oneOf/2.explanation: RC document: one initially uncharged series resistor and grounded capacitor, driven at t=0.

/oneOf/2/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis circuit document; it must be "schemaxis.ngspice/1". It is not the ngspice release.

/oneOf/2/properties/operation.explanation: Select dcSweep for steady signed voltage, acSweep for phasor response, or rcStep for initially uncharged first-order settling.

/oneOf/2/properties/circuit.explanation: The step-response network: exactly one resistor from the source node to a response node and exactly one capacitor from that response node to ground ("0"). No other components are allowed.

/oneOf/2/properties/circuit/properties/s.explanation: Non-ground node driven by the single ideal source referenced to node 0. Use a lowercase identifier; default in. The name gnd in any case is reserved because ngspice rewrites it to ground node 0; use 0 for ground or another name such as gnd1.

/oneOf/2/properties/circuit/properties/r.explanation: Exactly one resistor, between the source node and the response node (the capacitor's other terminal).
One ideal resistor with unique name, distinct endpoints and positive ohmic resistance.
Unique lowercase component identifier within the circuit. It labels the generated inspectable netlist; node 0 cannot be a component name.

First terminal node of this component: "0" is ground; any other node is a lowercase letter followed by up to 31 lowercase letters, digits or underscores. a and b must differ. The name gnd in any case is reserved because ngspice rewrites it to ground node 0; use 0 for ground or another name such as gnd1.
Second component endpoint, distinct from a. Uncoupled ideal R, C and L responses do not depend on endpoint ordering.
Positive resistance in ohms, 0.001 to 1e9. Changing resistance changes divider gain or the RC/RL time scale; singular or ill-conditioned networks are rejected.

/oneOf/2/properties/circuit/properties/c.explanation: Exactly one capacitor, from the response node to ground ("0"). Its capacitance times the resistance sets the time constant tau = R x C.
One ideal capacitor with unique name, distinct endpoints and positive capacitance in farads.
Unique lowercase component identifier within the circuit. It labels the generated inspectable netlist; node 0 cannot be a component name.

First terminal node of this component: "0" is ground; any other node is a lowercase letter followed by up to 31 lowercase letters, digits or underscores. a and b must differ. The name gnd in any case is reserved because ngspice rewrites it to ground node 0; use 0 for ground or another name such as gnd1.
Second component endpoint, distinct from a. Uncoupled ideal R, C and L responses do not depend on endpoint ordering.
Positive capacitance in farads, 1e-12 to 1. For example 1e-6 is one microfarad; changing C shifts cutoff and settling time.

/oneOf/2/properties/circuit/properties/p.explanation: Nodes to publish: the source node and/or the response node, without repeats. The capacitor voltage is on the response node.
pitfalls: With the default, the response node must be named "out".

/oneOf/2/properties/circuit/properties/p.explanation: A present non-ground node to publish; selected probe identifiers must be distinct. The name gnd in any case is reserved because ngspice rewrites it to ground node 0; use 0 for ground or another name such as gnd1.

/oneOf/2/properties/stop.explanation: End time of the step response in seconds (the start is always 0). It must lie between 0.01 and 20 time constants R x C; five time constants show about 99.3% of the final voltage.
pitfalls: With other R or C values the default 0.005 s may fall outside 0.01 to 20 tau and fail planning; set stop explicitly (for example 5 x R x C).

/oneOf/2/properties/points.explanation: Number of evenly spaced samples including both endpoints, 2 to 512. More points resolve the curve better; the requirements only see these samples.

/oneOf/2/properties/amplitude.explanation: Nonzero source phasor/step amplitude in volts, range -1000 to 1000, default 1. In AC amplitudeConvention explicitly interprets phasors as peak (default) or rms and controls power factor. Negative source amplitude reverses native voltage/current phasors while relative transfer phase and power remain consistent. rcStep uses the step height.

/oneOf/2/properties/requirements.explanation: Optional named acceptance requirements on checked native samples. A physically valid circuit may miss these bounds and fail with PERFORMANCE_NOT_MET; omitted requirements add no performance gate.

/oneOf/2/properties/requirements/items.explanation: One RC requirement: a name, a published probe, quantity voltage_V, axis time_s, a time window and at least one bound.

/oneOf/2/properties/requirements/items/p.explanation: Unique lowercase requirement identifier, up to 64 characters. It names a measured acceptance result and its explained next action.
Select a node already listed in circuit.probes. Requirements use actual independently checked native node voltages.
voltage_V: the probe's node voltage in volts at the sampled times. It is the only quantity available for rcStep.
Must be time_s: the window is given in seconds from the step.

Inclusive [lower, upper] range of the sweep axis, in seconds, over which the bounds are checked. It must lie inside the declared sweep and contain at least one sample; only those samples are tested. Endpoints equal to a sample coordinate are matched despite tiny floating-point rounding, but no tolerance is added to the voltage or gain bounds.
pitfalls: Behaviour between samples is not checked; increase points if a peak or crossing could fall between them.

/oneOf/2/properties/requirements/items/p.explanation: One finite sample coordinate in the stated axis units; the first is the inclusive lower endpoint, the second the inclusive upper endpoint.

Optional inclusive lower bound in the chosen quantity units. The smallest observed value is the worst lower-bound condition; signed margin is observed minus minimum. Magnitude quantities require nonnegative bounds; voltage, dB, phase and powers retain their signs.

Optional inclusive upper bound in the chosen quantity units. The largest observed value is the worst upper-bound condition; signed margin is maximum minus observed. At least one bound is required; minimum cannot exceed maximum.

/oneOf/2/properties/requirements/items/a.explanation: Lower-bound form: minimum is given, so the smallest sampled value in the window must be at least minimum; maximum may also be given.
Upper-bound form: maximum is given, so the largest sampled value in the window must not exceed maximum; minimum may also be given.

/properties/circuit/anyOf/1/properties/b.explanation: Optional list of up to eight existing component names for derived AC current phasors and passive active/reactive power. Omit for no branch output. Current is positive from authored a to b; reversing terminals reverses current but preserves absorbed power. Currents use verified terminal voltages and ideal R/C/L laws, rather than native device-current readback. All selected metrics together must fit 64 CSV columns.
A declared resistor, capacitor or inductor name, unique in this selection. Branch current is positive from its authored a terminal to b; this is a component identifier, not a node name. Example r1.

/properties/spacing.explanation: Frequency grid: linear (default) means points total including endpoints; decade/octave means nominal samples per frequency decade/octave. Octave and short-decade partial intervals may end below stop. Ngspice47 redistributes full-decade spans to include stop; inspect frequencyGrid.actualSamples and lastFrequency_Hz. At least 3 and at most 512 actual samples are required. Use enough density to resolve narrow features.

/properties/portMetrics.explanation: When true, save native source current and independently check -i(vdrive) against solved current and KCL before publishing $input current, derived input impedance and complex/apparent power. Default false omits these ten columns. Current enters the passive network; input impedance near zero current is undefined and rejected. Select fewer probes if the whole output exceeds 64 columns.

/properties/amplitudeConvention.explanation: Interpret all AC phasor magnitudes as peak (default) or rms. Native AC analysis supplies linear phasors without choosing physical amplitude convention. Peak uses S=V*conj(I)/2; rms uses S=V*conj(I). Switching convention preserves native voltages/currents and doubles powers. The declared convention and factor remain in the summary.
